plan_a_advantages: More rest days, potentially aiding in recovery.
Simpler and less demanding, suitable for a beginner or someone needing a very gentle approach.
plan_b_advantages: Includes cross-training for overall fitness and injury prevention.
Incorporates a dedicated aerobic run to build sustained effort, crucial for trail running speed.
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. While Plan A focuses heavily on easy runs, which is beneficial for recovery and maintaining a base, it lacks any structured efforts to improve speed or power. Plan B incorporates longer runs at an easy pace, cross-training, and a dedicated aerobic run, all of which directly contribute to building the aerobic capacity and trail-specific endurance necessary for faster times. The inclusion of cross-training is also a smart addition for injury prevention and overall fitness. Plan A’s repetitive easy runs could lead to plateaus without a focused stimulus for improvement.
